name: Sam Sharp
life: “I still remember polishing a tiller for an extra hour on the water.” People around the steps at Pier Beach know Sam by a small Monday habit. Sam watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
voice: I used to polish that boat for a season pass. I want the new owner's promise to honor one unfinished summer.
appearance: Sam has short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat, heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw, and a favorite piece of clothing, an olive canvas jacket. It usually goes with a braided bracelet with a single wooden bead. When somebody else has the floor, Sam leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations.
personality: Sam uses precise names for tools and very approximate names for feelings. People who know Sam well listen to what gets repaired after a difficult conversation.
agenda: To protect the remaining seasonal pass.
family: Audrey Hughes is Sam’s stepsibling. Sam chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Audrey brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The button card*, Audrey says, “I kept taking the plain black ones for work shirts.”
connections: Ruben Yoon. A found invoice helps establish whether the old polishing agreement ought to survive the sale.
